description: Classify the position of a single divider inside a grid, exercising boundary placements the native suite does not cover: an end-boundary divider on the first line, a far-edge divider on a line that is not completely filled (so it is not an end boundary), top and bottom dividers offset along the line, a single-span single-line grid, and end/bottom boundaries in a horizontal grid. A divider originates at zero-based coordinates and has its own orientation. Report seven independent boolean predicates describing whether the divider is the top, bottom, start, or end boundary; whether it is the first or last divider along the grid's main flow; and whether it is a side divider. A far boundary requires the relevant line to be completely filled. A vertical divider can never be a top or bottom boundary, and a horizontal divider can never be a start or end boundary.
